jess: Heads-up — after flipping on arch-aware kernel selection in autotuner I see p99 latency regressions for short sequences (<=32) under continuous batching in prod. 20-30% worse on T4 pools.
omar: ugh. can you paste the perf summary / flamegraph?
jess: quick flame + microbench below. noticed kernel switch from fused small-seq path -> generic matmul for certain batch sizes.
```
# perf summary (shortened)
p50: 18ms -> 17ms
p95: 45ms -> 48ms
p99: 120ms -> 156ms  <-- regression
comp: when seq<=32 and batch_size between 8-24, runtime chose generic gemm (launch overhead high)
KV-warm: cache hit ratio same
```
chloe: did autotuner change the launch mode? continuous batching can increase small-launch counts which kills short-paths.
alan: I remember we had a threshold: if avg_seq*batch > X choose fused-kernel; else choose generic. autotuner probably changed the cost model.
perf-bot: perf alert: hosted/t4 pool p99 increased 30% between 2026-03-01 02:00Z and 2026-03-01 03:30Z. Top contributors: kernel selection (42%), scheduling spikes (28%).
jess: repro script I used:
```
# repro loop
for b in 4 8 12 16 24; do
  run_microbench --model gpt-small --seq 16 --batch $b --continuous-batch --warm_kv 1
done
```
omar: try forcing the small-seq fused kernel to validate hypothesis: set KERNEL_FORCE=small_fused then rerun. if p99 drops we confirm.
alan: also inspect launch overhead timer: we have extra 20-30us for generic kernel due to additional memcpy+workspace init which scales with batch_count. continuous batching increases number of launches for the same effective throughput.
chloe: another angle: KV cache behavior. if we get more fragmented KV cache misses across concurrent requests, we end up with more filling and extra memsets before kernel -> increases tail. Did you check per-request kv miss rate?
jess: kv metrics: miss_rate ~ 2.1% same as baseline. but observed more frequent small-batch launches because scheduler now does tighter packing windows (max_wait_ms reduced by autotuner).
alan: so two interacting knobs: kernel pick (fused vs generic) and scheduling window. autotuner changed cost model and wait_ms -> ended up picking smaller wait_ms to lower avg latency but with continuous batching it forced more launches and exposed launch overhead for the non-fused kernel.
omar: proposed quick fixes: 1) add architecture-aware override: prefer fused-small for seq<=32 on T4/RTX when batch <= 32 2) revert autotuner scheduling change temporarily 3) add launch overhead term to the cost model so autotuner avoids configurations that create 2x more launches.
chloe: +1 add per-kernel launch_cost estimate to the profiler. we can get launch_cost by timing kernel enqueue->sync in microbench and store in cost table keyed by (arch, kernel_type, seq_len_range, batch_range).
```
# pseudo: cost table entry
{ "arch": "t4", "kernel": "small_fused", "seq": "<=32", "batch": "8-24", "launch_us": "45", "throughput_tok_s": "X" }
```
alan: also consider continuous batching heuristics: treat fused-kernel as amortizing launch overhead better so prefer it when estimated_launch_cost > threshold. autotuner should simulate number_of_launches = ceil(avg_tokens / kernel_token_capacity) to evaluate.
sre-bot: note: deploy risk for quick revert. we should gate revert to some canary capacity.
jess: ran forced-fused run: p99 back down to 118ms for same workload. forcing generic reproduces 150-160ms. so hypothesis confirmed.
omar: nice. next steps: 1) add launch_cost to autotuner model (PR) 2) quick canary override to prefer fused for seq<=32 on T4 3) add microbench job to CI that exercises mixed-batch regimes and records kernel picks 4) write a short runbook for oncall explaining this interaction.
chloe: I'll own the runbook + CI microbench. alan can you do PR for cost-model change? jess can you prepare canary config and smoke tests?
alan: yup. I will add the launch_cost field and a simulation pass to predict launches. aiming for PR today.
perf-bot: created perf ticket PERF-4289 linking traces and microbench logs.
jess: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility. i'll post follow-up with canary id and smoke numbers. :thumbsup:
